name: Basílica del Pilar – the unexploded bombs (Zaragoza)
story: Early in the war a Republican aircraft attacked Nationalist-held Zaragoza and dropped bombs on the Basilica of Our Lady of the Pillar, Spain's great Marian shrine. Bombs fell on the church and the square beside it, and none exploded. Nationalist propaganda presented this as a miracle, and the event became a strong symbol of the religious meaning Franco's side gave its war. Two of the bombs are still displayed inside the basilica.
see: Two defused bombs hang on a pillar inside the basilica. There is also a mark of the damage on the ceiling vaults.
plan: The basilica is open daily with free entry, so visit outside Mass times. The bombs are near the Holy Chapel of the Pillar.

boxes.text: The date, 3 August 1936, follows the standard study of the raid (J. Pujol Bertran, El bombardeo del templo del Pilar, 2023). Accounts differ on how many bombs fell, usually three or four.
